explanation: The main character in chapter 15, later known as Abraham, is a central figure in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
A title used to refer to God, the almighty Creator.
An agreement or commitment between two parties, here between God and Abram.
The area that God promises to give to Abram's descendants, later known as Canaan or the Promised Land.
A divine revelation or dream that provides insight or guidance.
An animal offered to God as part of a covenant or religious ceremony.
A ritual act in which smoke from burning offerings rises up to God as a symbolic gesture.
What will happen later; here it refers to prophecies about Abram's descendants and their destiny.
People who perform work or services for others, especially in a subordinate or servile relationship.
A reference to the Nile, the most important river in Egypt, symbolizing the future slavery of Abram's descendants in Egypt.
The period during which Abram's descendants will be oppressed and serve as slaves in Egypt.
God's just punishment or reward; here it refers to judgment upon the nations that oppress Abram's descendants.
An expression referring to Abram's descendants four generations later, when they will return to the Promised Land.
